$comment: The roles and recognition explainer (/roles/; /contributors/ redirects here). Unlisted: not linked from anywhere and kept out of search engines, for sharing by link with the board, coordinators and early ambassadors. Summarises the recognition-system draft (design/research/recognition-system.md), which the board hasn't approved yet. Only the ambassador program and its button exist today. [PLACEHOLDER] marks what's still open.
title: Roles and recognition
description: How people take part in The Upskilling Labs, and how the community recognizes them: public roles, and a merit system built on nomination. A working draft.
draft: A working draft for the board. Only the ambassador program and its button exist today; everything else here is what we're building toward.

hero.title: How people take part, and how we say thank you.
hero.lede: Some people give their time in a public role. Others improve the things everyone uses. Many do both. Here's how each is recognized.
hero.alt: The pin: the orb mark with teal and red cat-eye enamel

two.title: Time in a role. Work anyone can reuse.

items.label: Roles
items.title: Giving your time, in public.
items.body: Running a team, helping one, or talking to a room, in The Labs' name. Because it happens live, you're trained before you start, and each role has as many seats as the work needs.

items.label: Contributing
items.title: Improving what everyone uses.
items.body: A playbook, a flyer, a kit, a line of code. Anyone can suggest a change, any time, and it's reviewed before it's used. That's why contributing is open to everyone.

two.bridge: Practice connects the two. You can only review work in a role you've done yourself, so the merit ranks start with experience in the roles.

roles.title: Four roles to start.
roles.lede: Each role has two stages. Trained: you've done the role's orientation and you're seated. Practitioner: you've done the work for a while, and the role's lead confirms it.

items.name: Upskiller
items.does: Takes part in a Build Cycle: a few months on a small team (a pod), working on a real local problem.
items.practitioner: Builder: has made a confirmed contribution to the problem they worked on.

items.name: Poderator
items.does: Leads a pod through a Build Cycle, keeping the team on track and making sure everyone's heard.
items.trained: Trained and seated with a pod.
items.practitioner: Has led a pod through a full cycle.

items.name: Mentor
items.does: An experienced practitioner who helps pods when they get stuck, for one workshop or a whole cycle.
items.practitioner: Has mentored through a full cycle.

items.name: Ambassador
items.does: Tells their own story, invites people to their first workshop, and gives one talk to a room.
items.trained: Finishes orientation and gets the Ambassador button.
items.practitioner: Has passed it on: [N] new people, one talk, and one new ambassador.

roles.buttonNote: Each role gets its own button when it launches. The Ambassador button is the first. How the Practitioner stage is marked is still being designed.
roles.notRoles: Advisors and neighborhood committee members are appointed, not trained, so they'll be recognized differently. [PLACEHOLDER]

open.title: Anyone can contribute.
open.body: Contributor isn't a rank. If you improve a playbook, a flyer, or the code, you're a contributor, credited by name. No application, no gate.

ranks.title: Recognized by peers, one step at a time.
ranks.lede: Every Contributing Member wears the same pin. Each rank adds a ring around it, for people who've done the work in more than one role and are trusted by those who already hold the rank.
ranks.member: The pin on its own is the Contributing Member pin: given for work The Labs runs on, with no formal requirement. The first ones go to our two steering committees.
ranks.more: See the pin and its rings up close

items.name: Reviewer
items.nominated: Two people who already hold the rank sponsor you, from different roles or different Labs.
items.can: Review suggested changes, and new Practitioners, in the roles you've practised. Sponsor new Reviewers.

items.name: Committer
items.recognizes: Has helped across every core area of The Labs.
items.nominated: Sponsored by Committers, and recorded by HQ.
items.can: Approve changes to their Lab's playbooks, sign off Practitioners, run a Build Cycle or workshop series, within a written grant from the board.

items.name: Maintainer
items.nominated: Nominated by Maintainers, confirmed by the board.
items.can: Shape the standard for their area, with the board keeping the final say.

ranks.metal: Brass for your region. Silver for work across the whole network.
ranks.areasNote: The board sets the core areas. [PLACEHOLDER]
ranks.names: Rank names are drafts, borrowed from open-source projects, until the board decides. [PLACEHOLDER]

alt.reviewer: The pin with one brushed brass ring around it
alt.committer: The pin with two brushed brass rings around it
alt.maintainer: The pin with three brushed brass rings around it

nomination.title: How someone is recognized.
nomination.lede: Recognition always starts with the work, and always comes from peers. The award is recorded first; the ceremony follows.

steps.title: Do the work.
steps.body: Become a Practitioner in the roles the rank asks for.

steps.title: Two sponsors.
steps.body: Two people who already hold the rank put you forward, from different roles or Labs, so no one is recognized inside one small circle.

steps.title: Checked and recorded.
steps.body: Your Lab nominates, and HQ checks the criteria and records it on the register. For Maintainers, the board confirms.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next regional gathering, held every few months. Your sponsors pin it on and say a sentence about what you did.

seats.title: The rank is yours. Permissions come with a seat.

items.title: Ranks are permanent.
items.body: A pin records what you've done, and it stays with you.

items.title: Seats carry permissions.
items.body: Each Lab keeps as many active seats as the work needs. The register shows who's active now, not the pin.

items.title: Emeritus is an honor.
items.body: Step back whenever you need to. You keep the rank, the title and your voice, and you can return to any open seat.

guardrails.title: A few things that don't change.
items: No one can buy a rank, a pin, or a vote. Supporting Members, who pay light dues, get their own button and nothing more.
Ranks carry no vote in how The Labs is governed. The boards run programs, money and the brand.
Recognition isn't certification. It's the community saying thank you, and it never implies vetting The Labs hasn't done.
The one exception to permanence is a serious breach of the Code of Conduct.
